domain_restrictions: d is a nonnegative real number
d defines the closed interval with endpoints 0 and d: the interval is from 0 to d
f is differentiable at every point of that closed interval in the stated sense
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every function f from reals to reals and every nonnegative real number d, if f is differentiable on the closed interval from 0 to d, then f(d) minus f(0) equals the interval integral from 0 to d of the derivative of f.

for all nonnegative real numbers d
if f is differentiable on the closed interval from 0 to d, then ...

statement_nl: Let f : ℝ → ℝ and let d be a nonnegative real number. If f is differentiable on the closed interval [0,d], then f(d) - f(0) equals the interval integral from 0 to d of its derivative.
